records.title: How to Add Audio to Video with Claude MCP and Medux
records.description: Step-by-step tutorial for adding an audio track to a silent video with Claude, MCP, and Medux, including upload URLs, curl commands, task polling, and MP4 download.
records.prompt: Use the connected Medux tools to replace or add the audio track on the attached SOURCE_VIDEO with the attached SOURCE_AUDIO. Preserve the video resolution and duration. Show me both upload file IDs and the proposed add-audio arguments, then wait for my approval. After approval, monitor the Medux task and return the completed MP4.

records.title: How to Add a Logo Watermark to Video with Codex MCP and Medux
records.description: Learn how Codex uses Medux through MCP to upload a video and logo, place a watermark, monitor the task, and download the final branded MP4.
records.prompt: Use Medux to add logo2.png to sample.mp4. Resize the logo to an appropriate size and place it in the top-right corner of the video.

records.title: How to Add a Logo to Video with Claude MCP and Medux
records.description: Claude MCP tutorial for adding a logo watermark to a video with Medux, from uploading the video and logo to choosing placement and downloading the finished MP4.
records.prompt: Prompt used in Claude Use Medux to add logo.png to sample.mp4. Resize the logo to an appropriate size and place it in the top-right corner of the video. Upload the files using the curl command.

records.title: How to Adjust Audio Pitch with Claude MCP and Medux
records.description: A Claude MCP and Medux tutorial for changing audio pitch, creating higher and lower pitch versions, uploading files with curl, polling tasks, and downloading MP3 results.
records.prompt: project/ └── sample-audio.m4a The workflowDescribe the taskCreate upload URLUpload audioRun two pitch shiftsDownload results 01Describe both pitch changes in one promptAsk Claude to use Medux and specify the exact change for each output. In the tutorial, the source file is shifted up by 100% and down by 50%.Use Medux to modify the pitch of sample-audio.m4a. Create two outputs: - Increase pitch by 100% (2× frequency / +12 semitones) - Decrease pitch by 50% (0.5× frequency / −12 semitones) Upload the file with curl when needed.

records.title: How to Replace a Video Character with Claude MCP and Medux
records.description: Step-by-step Claude MCP tutorial for replacing a character in video with Medux using a source clip, reference image, upload URLs, task polling, and final video download.
records.prompt: Use the connected Medux tools to replace the character in the attached SOURCE_VIDEO with the character shown in the attached REFERENCE_IMAGE. Preserve the original motion, framing, duration, and audio. Show me the uploaded file IDs and exact replacement arguments, then wait for my approval. After approval, monitor the task and return the completed video.

records.title: How to Replace a Video Character with Codex MCP and Medux
records.description: Use Codex MCP and Medux to replace a character in a video, including file upload, reference character image, task submission, status polling, and final MP4 download.
records.prompt: Using the connected Medux MCP server, replace the character in SOURCE_VIDEO with the character in REFERENCE_IMAGE. Inspect and upload both workspace files, preserve the original motion, framing, duration, and audio, and show me the exact tool arguments. Wait for my approval, then monitor the task, save the result in this workspace, and verify its duration.

records.prompt: /Users/chuan/projects/test_mudex/remove_subtitle.mp4 The tutorial starts with one local MP4 file and a simple Codex request. 02 Ask Codex to remove the visible subtitles Keep the instruction direct. Tell Codex which file to use, what result you want, and that it should call Medux through MCP instead of doing unnecessary local analysis. Remove all visible subtitles from the video located at /Users/chuan/projects/test_mudex/remove_subtitle.mp4 and output a clean version without subtitles. Use Medux. Call the Medux MCP directly and do not perform excessive analysis.

records.title: How to Restore Old Photos with Codex MCP and Medux
records.description: Codex MCP and Medux tutorial for restoring old photos, from local image upload to restoration task submission, status tracking, and repaired image download.
records.prompt: Using the connected Medux MCP server, restore OLD_PHOTO in this workspace. Repair scratches, fading, and contrast while preserving identity and composition. Inspect and upload the image, show me the photo-repair arguments, then wait for my approval. After approval, monitor the task, save the result locally, and compare its dimensions with the source.

records.title: How to Clone a Voice and Generate Speech with Codex MCP and Medux
records.description: Use Codex MCP and Medux for voice cloning and text-to-speech, including reference audio upload, text input, task polling, and local WAV download.
records.prompt: /Users/chuan/projects/test_mudex/ ├── reference_voice.wav # Reference voice used for cloning ├── tts.txt # Text to synthesize └── config/ For best results, use a clear human voice recording with minimal background noise. Keep the target script in tts.txt. Step-by-step guide 01 Configure the Medux MCP Server in Codex Open Codex settings, go to MCP servers, and add or update the Medux MCP server. In the video, the configuration uses a remote MCP endpoint and an Authorization header. Once connected, Medux capabilities such as file upload, voice cloning, status polling, and speech synthesis become callable tools inside Codex. Configure Medux under MCP servers. The API token in this screenshot has been redacted. 02 Ask Codex to clone and synthesize the voice Return to the test_mudex project and describe the task in natural language. Include the reference audio path and the text file path. Codex will inspect the files and choose the relevant Medux MCP tools. Use Medux MCP to clone the voice from the reference audio file /Users/chuan/projects/test_mudex/reference_voice.wav and synthesize speech using the text contained in /Users/chuan/projects/test_mudex/tts.txt.
